paper.title: Estimating ETS parameters: smooth and statsforecast on simulated data

declarations.competing_interests: The guarantor is the author and maintainer of the smooth package, one of the two implementations evaluated.

definitions.definition:
smooth 1.2.0 ES(model=<form>, initial='optimal', loss='likelihood', bounds='usual'). Each fits the data-generating form (no model selection), with the same innovations-form equations as the generating process, for the form fixed to the generating one:
$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ b_t &= b_{t-1} + \beta\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + s_{t-m} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ s_t &= s_{t-m} + \gamma\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$
with the smoothing parameters $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ estimated by maximum likelihood of the Gaussian innovations model. The initial states are estimated jointly with the smoothing parameters. Parameter bounds: bounds='usual'.

smooth 1.2.0 ES(model=<form>, initial='backcasting', loss='likelihood', bounds='usual'), smooth's default. Each fits the data-generating form (no model selection), with the same innovations-form equations as the generating process, for the form fixed to the generating one:
$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ b_t &= b_{t-1} + \beta\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + s_{t-m} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ s_t &= s_{t-m} + \gamma\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$
with the smoothing parameters $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ estimated by maximum likelihood of the Gaussian innovations model. The initial states are obtained by backcasting; only the smoothing parameters are optimised. Parameter bounds: bounds='usual'.

statsforecast 2.1.1 AutoETS(season_length=m, model=<form>, damped=False) with the form fixed to the generating one (no selection). Each fits the data-generating form (no model selection), with the same innovations-form equations as the generating process, for the form fixed to the generating one:
$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ b_t &= b_{t-1} + \beta\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + s_{t-m} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ s_t &= s_{t-m} + \gamma\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$
with the smoothing parameters $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ estimated by maximum likelihood of the Gaussian innovations model. The initial states are optimised jointly with the smoothing parameters. Bounds: lower 1e-4 and upper 0.9999 for $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$, with $\beta\le\alpha$, $\gamma\le 1-\alpha$ and admissibility.

Simulated series from ETS in its innovations form with additive Gaussian errors $\varepsilon_t \sim N(0,1)$ independent, started from $l_0=100$, $b_0=1$ and seasonal indices $s_j=10\sin(2\pi j/12)$ for $j=0,\dots,11$, with no burn-in. Three forms:

ETS(A,N,N):
$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$
ETS(A,A,N):
$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + b_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ b_t &= b_{t-1} + \beta\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$
ETS(A,N,A) with period $m=12$:
$$\begin{aligned} y_t &= l_{t-1} + s_{t-m} + \varepsilon_t \\ l_t &= l_{t-1} + \alpha\,\varepsilon_t \\ s_t &= s_{t-m} + \gamma\,\varepsilon_t \end{aligned}$$
Parameter settings: ETS(A,N,N) with $\alpha=0.1$ and with $\alpha=0.5$; ETS(A,A,N) with $(\alpha,\beta)=(0.3,0.05)$ and with $(0.5,0.2)$; ETS(A,N,A) with $(\alpha,\gamma)=(0.2,0.1)$. Together the five settings have 8 parameter cells (setting and smoothing parameter). Series lengths $T\in\{50,100,250,500\}$, 300 replicates per setting and length. Each setting and length has its own random stream, seeded from the run seed, the setting index and $T$.
Mean over successful replicates of the estimate minus the true value of a smoothing parameter, for one method, setting and series length.
Square root of the mean over successful replicates of the squared (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
Mean over successful replicates of the absolute value of (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.

Consistency of an estimator in the sense used here: the RMSE of a smoothing parameter estimate is lower at series length $T=500$ than at $T=50$ in a given setting. This checks the direction of change between two lengths, not the rate of convergence or the limit.

For a setting, smoothing parameter and series length: the RMSE of smooth ES with optimised initial states divided by the RMSE of statsforecast AutoETS. There are 32 such cells (8 parameter cells, 4 lengths).

A replicate whose estimate of a smoothing parameter lies within $10^{-3}$ of a lower or upper bound of its admissible region (for $\beta$: $0$ or $\alpha$; for $\gamma$: $0$ or $1-\alpha$; for $\alpha$: $0$ or $1$), counted as in the run's script.

assessments.rationale: The criterion compares only two lengths, and in the ETS(A,N,A) gamma cell the RMSE of smooth barely falls and many estimates lie on a bound (L1); the result does not show convergence to zero. A web search found no formal earlier simulation study of this comparison.

claims.statement: The smooth ES and statsforecast AutoETS arms both maximise the Gaussian likelihood of the innovations form (smooth loss='likelihood', statsforecast opt_crit='lik').

The smoothing parameters $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ have the same meaning in smooth ES and statsforecast AutoETS (the innovations form of the generating process), so that estimates of both are compared with the true values without conversion.

evidence.description: Run RN2 of the lab record (script `files/sim.py`, command `sim.py --seed 20261111 --R 300 --T 50 100 250 500`), under plan PL1 fixed before the run. For each of five ETS data-generating settings and four series lengths, 300 series were simulated; each was fitted by smooth ES with optimised initial states, smooth ES with backcasting and statsforecast AutoETS, with the model form fixed to the generating one. Bias, RMSE and MAE of each smoothing-parameter estimate around the true value were computed over replicates. No fit failed. Estimates on a bound are counted (an estimate within 0.001 of a bound), not dropped. The full-precision results of the run are in `files/ets-estimation.results.csv`. R was 300, so the 20-minute reduction to 200 did not apply. A first pilot run (RN1, 10 replicates) was exploratory and is not used by any claim.

simulation.model: ETS(A,N,N), ETS(A,A,N) and ETS(A,N,A) in innovations form with Gaussian errors, simulated and refitted with each of three arms (D1, D2, D3)
simulation.runs: Run RN2 of the lab record: 5 settings x 4 series lengths x 300 replicates x 3 arms
simulation.seeds: 20261111, combined with the setting index and the series length to seed each cell

limitations.statement: In the ETS(A,N,A) setting the estimates of gamma often lie on a bound: at series length 500, 286 of 300 replicates for smooth ES with backcasting, 118 for smooth ES with optimised initials and 25 for statsforecast AutoETS; the bias of the smooth estimates stays near -0.09 and -0.06, and the cause (bounds, parametrisation or the optimiser) was not investigated.

Each package was run in one version (smooth 1.2.0, statsforecast 2.1.1) with the model form fixed to the generating one and default optimiser settings, so the results do not transfer to other versions or to automatic model selection.

The guarantor is the author and maintainer of the smooth package under evaluation; the simulation design and the analysis were fixed in a plan before the run, and every result is recorded, including those against smooth.
